solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Monkey unfortunately gets African antelopes

parts.note: a monkey, like an imp, is a mischievous little rascal
alas is an exclamation of regret, saying things went badly

explanation.surface: A monkey has the bad luck to meet a herd of antelopes on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' looks like the animal but stands for a cheeky child; 'gets' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalas are graceful reddish antelopes of the African grasslands, a plural to match the definition.

clue.text: Sell fine piece of wood

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
a log is a piece of a tree trunk

explanation.surface: A trader offers a choice bit of timber for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: To flog is informal British for to sell, often hard or cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for hawking goods, especially pushing them hard on buyers.

clue.text: Have dinner hosted by good French portrait photographer

indicators.note: being hosted by something puts the guest inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: bon is the French word for good
to eat is to have a meal such as dinner

explanation.surface: An invitation to dine with a fine French photographer of portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Beaton was a celebrated English society and royal portrait photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Beaton made his name shooting society figures and the royal family in formal studio sittings.

clue.text: Money one accountant needed for certain plants

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
I is the Roman numeral for one
CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Funds and a bookkeeper are required to buy some garden plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass for money is northern English slang; Brassica is the cabbage genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the genus covering cabbages, kale, sprouts and mustards, a particular group of plants.

clue.text: Dogged girl is flighty — she's after rich mate

indicators.note: something flighty is capricious and unstable, so these letters fly into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A persistent but fickle young woman pursues a wealthy husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is flighty' rearranges the ten letters of DOGGED GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold-digger is slang for someone who courts a partner purely for wealth.

clue.text: Stray animal originally taken in by fixer

indicators.note: being taken in by something places the piece within it

parts.note: a mender is someone who fixes or repairs things

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word animal, its first letter

explanation.surface: A lost animal is adopted by a repairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like an adjective for the animal but is the verb, to wander off course.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly, drifting from a direct route like a winding river.

clue.text: Steelworks made a stink on the outskirts of Exeter

parts.note: smelt is the British past tense of smell, to give off a stink

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: An industrial plant on the edge of Exeter gave off a foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelter is a works where ore is melted to extract metal, much like a steel mill.

clue.text: Dishonest man on board in last month returned

indicators.note: in places the chess piece inside the other letters
returned means the month's short form is read backwards

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the final month of the year
a rook is a piece, or man, on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A crooked fellow aboard ship came back at the end of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked is a common synonym for corrupt or underhand in dealings.

clue.text: Boozer, male, associated with ex-President

parts.note: a bull is a male bovine, elephant or whale
and joins things associated together
George Bush, father or son, is a former US President

explanation.surface: A drinking man links up with a former American president.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer is British slang for a pub; the Old Bull and Bush is a well-known pub in Hampstead, London.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer in British slang is a pub, and this one is a famous London tavern celebrated in a music-hall song.

clue.text: Mao Tse-tung cooked vegetables

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Chinese leader prepared a dish of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters of MAO TSE-TUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetouts are flat pea pods eaten whole, a type of green vegetable.

clue.text: Dingy English seaside feature

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A drab English seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A dune is a sand hill formed by wind along a beach.

clue.text: Fashion designer a liberal authority in church

parts.note: Pierre Cardin was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A couturier is a progressive figure within the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is a senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church, ranked just below the Pope.

clue.text: Prediction of small return on investment by state

parts.note: divi is informal British for a dividend, a payout from shares
a nation is a country or state

explanation.surface: A forecast that a country will yield only a modest profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Divi is a British colloquial shortening of dividend.
explanation.definitionFit: Divination is foretelling the future by supernatural means, a form of forecasting.

clue.text: Van Gogh painting is about to go up

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to rise is to go up

explanation.surface: Someone says a Van Gogh is about to increase in value.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a forecast that a painting's value will climb; 'about' is really the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises is the 1889 canvas by Van Gogh depicting a bed of blue flowers.

clue.text: He wrote novels when vaguely befuddled

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An author wrote his books while in a hazy, confused state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' rearranges WHEN VAGUELY; Evelyn Waugh wrote Brideshead Revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh was an English novelist, author of Decline and Fall and Brideshead Revisited.

clue.text: A rapidly developing jeweller

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters change shape into a new form

explanation.surface: A gem cutter whose skills are growing fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges A RAPIDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapidary is a craftsman who cuts, polishes or engraves gemstones.

clue.text: Some hippopotamus I call Oliver perhaps

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone names a hippo Oliver.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage show based on Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver! is a famous stage show with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Great number wanting starter with full-flavoured exotic meat

indicators.note: wanting its starter means losing the opening letter

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
rich food is full-flavoured and heavy

explanation.surface: A large party goes without a first course but has a rich foreign meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but it is the first letter of HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostrich is a lean red meat from the large flightless bird, unusual on most menus.

clue.text: Suggestion about container for vegetable

indicators.note: about means round, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion
an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A hint about which pot to use for a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a white root crop of the cabbage family eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Bath switched lock and prop

indicators.note: switched means the letters are turned round end to end

parts.note: a tub is a bath
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: In a city in Somerset, someone swapped a padlock and a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the Somerset city but is a tub; 'lock' is hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a structure built against a wall to support it.

clue.text: Worked after time, fuel being sent to eastern Germany

indicators.note: after places the fuel following the time letter

parts.note: oil is a fuel
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone did overtime while fuel was shipped to the former East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern Germany' suggests the old GDR but splits into E and D; 'being sent to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To have toiled is to have laboured hard, a synonym for worked.

clue.text: One will punch son in display of temper maybe

indicators.note: in places the son's letter inside the outburst

parts.note: a fit of temper is an outburst

explanation.surface: A son throws a tantrum and lashes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fist is the clenched hand used to throw blows, so it is the thing that strikes.

clue.text: Italy's smooth source of elixir consumed by TT — it'll raise spirits

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the other piece

parts.note: TT means teetotal, and a teetotal place is dry
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
still water is calm and smooth

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Italy's finest elixir is drunk by a teetotaller who says it lifts the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise spirits' sounds like cheering someone up, but a distillery produces spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery is a plant that makes whisky, gin and other alcoholic spirits.

clue.text: Metal electrical wire

definitions.meaning: a soft heavy grey metallic element, symbol Pb
a flex or cable connecting an appliance to the mains

explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy grey metal, and also the British term for an electrical flex or cable.

clue.text: Woman engages lad for building work

indicators.note: engages means takes on or holds inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name
a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A woman hires a boy to do some construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is stonework or brickwork, the craft of building with stone.

clue.text: Last character driven from pirates' home in atonement

indicators.note: driven from means expelled, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta is The Pirates of Penzance, a Cornish port
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The last person thrown out of the pirates' base must make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, made famous by The Pirates of Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is a voluntary act of self-punishment done to make amends for wrongdoing.
